title: UK Budget 2026: Lower Going Rates, Two-Year Graduate Visa for Some
excerpt: The Budget promises 25th-percentile going rates from spring 2027, a two-year Graduate visa for graduates of qualifying universities, and an HPI route widened to the top 150 institutions — but the general threshold will rise, the PhD discount will go, and most detail is still unpublished.
body:
• From spring 2027, Skilled Worker occupation-specific going rates will be calculated at the 25th percentile of wages instead of the median, under Budget 2026 — but the general threshold, currently £41,700, will be uprated on 2026 wage data, with the new figure not yet announced.
  • Nothing has changed yet: current rules still require the higher of £41,700 or your occupation's going rate, and the Budget measures need Immigration Rules changes before they can be relied on.
  • The Graduate visa will be set at two years for graduates of high-compliance universities with strong labour market outcomes; under published rules it otherwise falls to 18 months from 1 January 2027, while PhD graduates keep three years.
  • The High Potential Individual route will expand to graduates of the top 150 global institutions, with a proportional increase to its cap — no start date has been announced.

Budget 2026, published on 28 October 2026, commits the UK government to what it calls the most pro-business migration system in Europe for high-skill workers. For Indian professionals and students the package mixes genuine easing, offsetting increases, and detail not yet published.

Who is affected — exactly

The changes concern Skilled Worker applicants, international students planning to use the Graduate route, and recent graduates of top-ranked non-UK universities using the unsponsored High Potential Individual (HPI) route. They change nothing for anyone applying today. Legal analyses by Hill Dickinson and Paragon Law stress that most measures require Immigration Rules amendments first.

What changed, precisely — Skilled Worker salaries

Under the current rules, a Skilled Worker must usually be paid the higher of the general threshold of £41,700 a year or the going rate for the occupation, as set out on the GOV.UK Skilled Worker visa page. Since April 2024 the going rate has been benchmarked to median earnings. The Budget 2026 document states that, from spring 2027, the government will implement the Migration Advisory Committee's recommendations: reducing occupation-specific minimum salary thresholds from the median to the 25th percentile of wages, uprating the general threshold based on 2026 wage data, updating thresholds annually using the latest ONS wage data, levelling new entrant discounts into a single figure for those studying, recently graduated or in professional training, and removing the PhD discount.

The mechanism matters. A lower going rate only helps where the going rate is the binding constraint; where the general threshold is higher, the uprated general threshold — whose new amount has not been announced — will decide instead, Hill Dickinson noted. On new entrants, the current rule allows sponsorship at at least £33,400 and 70 percent of the going rate in specified circumstances; the MAC recommended a single new entrant threshold of £33,400, Paragon Law reported, but the detailed rules are unpublished and £33,400 should not be assumed universal. Employers relying on the PhD discount should plan for its removal, both firms advised.

Graduate visa and HPI route

For the Graduate route, the baseline is already in law. The GOV.UK Graduate visa guidance states the visa lasts two years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027, and three years for a PhD or other doctoral qualification, with a £937 application fee plus a healthcare surcharge of usually £1,035 per year. Against that scheduled cut, the Budget states the Graduate visa duration will be set at two years for individuals who graduate from high-compliance universities where there are strong labour market outcomes. The government has not yet identified which universities qualify, Hill Dickinson noted, so no graduate can yet know whether they are in the two-year group.

For HPI, the Budget states the route will expand to applicants with eligible qualifications from the top 150 of the world's best institutions, with a proportional increase to the cap under the scheme. The route is unsponsored, so employers can hire eligible graduates without a sponsor licence. No start date has been announced, Hill Dickinson noted.

When — and the one immediate change

The salary changes are scheduled from spring 2027; the extended curtailment period — up to six months for the highest-skilled sponsored workers, replacing the current 60 days for those in scope — is slated for 2027; and no dates have been given for the Graduate or HPI changes. One measure is already dated: employer payments of the Immigration Skills Charge and Certificate of Sponsorship fee will not be a taxable benefit in kind for payments on or after 28 October 2026, though it still needs the Finance Bill 2026-27, Hill Dickinson says.

What to do next

Apply under today's rules: check your salary against the higher of £41,700 and your occupation's going rate on the GOV.UK Skilled Worker page, and do not price a spring 2027 application on the 25th-percentile rate until the new salary tables and the uprated general threshold are published. If you are finishing a UK degree, the published Graduate rules give you a concrete deadline: an application on or before 31 December 2026 secures two years under current guidance, checked on the GOV.UK Graduate visa page — apply before your Student visa expires and after your provider has told the Home Office you completed your course. Waiting carries a specific risk: the 18-month Graduate duration takes effect on 1 January 2027 for those outside the as-yet-undefined qualifying universities.

nri_angle: Indians are among the largest cohorts on the UK's Skilled Worker, Graduate and HPI routes, so the spring 2027 move to 25th-percentile going rates, the two-year Graduate visa for qualifying universities, and the HPI expansion to the top 150 institutions directly shape whether Indian graduates can stay, switch and settle in Britain.
